Question: Can rapamycin reverse memory deficits linked to reduced Tsc2 function?
response: In this animal work, giving the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin to adult female Tsc2 heterozygous mice reversed their object memory deficits [1]. The Tsc2 gene normally restrains mTOR signaling, so when Tsc2 levels fall mTOR signaling becomes overactive in both rodents and humans, and inhibiting mTOR appears to correct the associated memory problem [1]. The study also depleted microglia using PLX5622 and confirmed a substantial loss of microglia as part of probing immune contributions to the phenotype [1]. This is a preclinical mouse study, so the memory benefit may not translate directly to humans. (PMID 38255309; Biomedicines, 2024; DOI 10.3390/biomedicines12010203) This is educational information, not diagnosis or treatment, and clinical decisions belong to a licensed clinician or pharmacist.
